LESSON: WRITING 10.5.1 FILLING FORMS: APPLICATION FORMS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.5: Writing 10.5.1 Filling Forms: Application Forms

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 10.5.1 Filling Forms: Application Forms. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to fill in all parts of a form?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise bursary and scholarship application forms from a list of forms
2. value the importance of giving accurate and sufficient information in forms

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 10.5.1 FILLING FORMS: APPLICATION FORMS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 10.5.1 Filling Forms: Application Forms helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 10.5.1 FILLING FORMS: APPLICATION FORMS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Recognise bursary and scholarship application forms from a list of forms

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise bursary and scholarship application forms from a list of forms. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise bursary and scholarship application forms from a list of forms.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 10.5.1 Filling Forms: Application Forms”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise bursary and scholarship application forms from a list of forms. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Value the importance of giving accurate and sufficient information in forms

What this means
In this part you learn to value the importance of giving accurate and sufficient information in forms. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the importance of giving accurate and sufficient information in forms.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 10.5.1 Filling Forms: Application Forms to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the importance of giving accurate and sufficient information in forms. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 10.5.1 Filling Forms: Application Forms is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 10.5.1 Filling Forms: Application Forms”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recognise bursary and scholarship application forms from a list of forms)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 10.5.1 Filling Forms: Application Forms to a partner. (skill: value the importance of giving accurate and sufficient information in forms)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 10.5.1 Filling Forms: Application Forms to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognise bursary and scholarship application forms from a list of forms.
3. Practise this skill: value the importance of giving accurate and sufficient information in forms.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 10.5.1 Filling Forms: Application Forms from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 10.5.1 Filling Forms: Application Forms: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Writing 10.5.1 Filling Forms: Application Forms?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to fill in all parts of a form?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 10.5.1 Filling Forms: Application Forms means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognise bursary and scholarship application forms from a list of forms.
5. Be able to: value the importance of giving accurate and sufficient information in forms.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
